Cairn stops waiting to be told. It captures the work an agent is already doing,
consolidates it into durable knowledge without being asked, and hands that
knowledge back when the next session opens — with the server, not your laptop,
as the authority on what is true.

Still an **alpha**. Nothing here is a stability promise.

## Highlights

**Memory you do not have to write.** Previous releases remembered what you told
them to remember. This one watches the session: a failing test, the edit that
fixed it, a command that keeps working, a decision you stated and then acted on.
Those become durable knowledge on their own. No tool call, no prompt, no
`cairn remember` — and every record still says what evidence stands behind it.

**The server is the authority.** Durable knowledge lives on the server, and the
daemon becomes a client that renders what the server selected and reports what
it transmitted. When the server cannot be reached, Cairn says so and keeps
working locally rather than inventing an answer. What each side is allowed to
decide is now a property of the architecture, not of which code path ran.

**Knowledge comes back on its own.** When a session opens, Cairn delivers the
knowledge relevant to that project into the agent's context automatically, within
a budget. You do not ask for it.

**Three kinds of knowledge, each with the right authority.** Project knowledge is
shared by everyone working on the repository. **Personal** knowledge follows your
account across your own devices and is private to it. **Team** knowledge is
proposed by any member and made authoritative only by an administrator —
proposed, ratified, retired, with the actor recorded at each step. Personal and
team knowledge are new in this release; neither carries a project identifier, an
evidence reference or a verification claim, because neither is about a project.

**Your words do not leave your machine.** Semantic material crosses the local
privacy boundary as structured tokens that the session's own evidence already
justifies — never as prose. A prompt fragment, a file's contents, a credential:
none of them are things Cairn can send, because the boundary only admits tokens
it can independently re-derive from events already accepted.

## What changed since alpha.5

### Capture and consolidation

- Hooks emit safe canonical events through a local privacy screen, spool them
  durably, and deliver them when the server is reachable. A capture that misses
  its deadline is dropped rather than delaying your agent, and **the drop is now
  counted** instead of vanishing — `cairn status` shows it.
- A session's events are consolidated into durable records by deterministic
  rules. Nothing here needs a model, an embedding or a vector store.
- **A session's events now carry the order they actually happened in.** Each hook
  is a separate short-lived process, and under load two hooks the agent ran in
  order could be recorded out of order — which is invisible, because nothing is
  missing. A rule that reads a sequence ("tests were failing, this changed, they
  passed") then saw a session that never happened and recorded nothing. Ordering
  is now established where it is still true, and costs the agent no latency.
- A decline caused by Cairn's own deadline is reported as a deadline, not as a
  judgement about your content. Those are different problems with different
  remedies.

### Sync, servers and correctness

- **`cairn status` tells the truth about why delivery is stuck.** It takes a
  fresh, bounded, read-only reading of who is answering your server endpoint
  rather than trusting what some earlier daemon happened to observe. Replacing a
  server deployment no longer leaves Cairn reporting "no mismatch" while the
  entire backlog is queued for a server that is gone. Detection still works with
  no network at all.
- Work queued for one server deployment is held, not misdelivered, when the
  deployment behind your endpoint changes.
- **A queued item authored by one account is never submitted as another.** Sign
  in as someone else on a shared machine and your colleague's undelivered work
  waits for them instead of going out under your name.
- `cairn sync now` reports, per lane, which account it filtered by, what moved,
  what it withheld and why — six different situations that used to render
  identically as `applied 0`.

### Team knowledge

- Team entries carry a revision allocated in commit order, so a client can no
  longer advance past a change that lands a moment later and never see it again.
  A retirement that goes missing is permanent; this is what prevents it.
- A retirement or ratification records who acted, on every device, and a
  transition that was not actually recorded now fails instead of reporting
  success.
- Team ingest ignores lifecycle fields carried by a sync payload — establishing a
  retirement is an administrator's act, not a queued row's.

### Security — please read if you run a server

Five holes in the sync and link paths are closed. Together they were a complete
chain: register an account on a public route, look a project up by its public Git
remote, join it by naming its identifier, then read and write everything in it.

- Self-registration and self-join are gone. An operator creates accounts with
  `cairn-server users add`.
- Project discovery is scoped to the memberships of the caller.
- Tombstones and sync upserts carry a project predicate, so one project's records
  can no longer overwrite or delete another's.

**If you have run a Cairn server reachable by anyone you do not trust, review its
accounts and memberships after upgrading.** Cairn cannot tell you retroactively
whether the chain was used.

### Privacy

- A deleted project keeps contributing privacy identities. Deletion is soft and
  leaves the project's name in place, so narrowing the screen would start
  accepting exactly the disclosure it exists to refuse. The command path and the
  ingest path now read one source, so they cannot disagree about the same text.

### Reliability and platforms

- Several Windows-specific faults are fixed, all of the same shape: a file with a
  live handle cannot be deleted on Windows the way it can on Unix, and code that
  assumed otherwise discarded the error. Cairn's own Windows integration suite is
  green.
- A store that cannot be opened now names the file and the budget it exceeded
  instead of reporting an internal pool error.

### Web and operations

- The web console's lint, type-check and end-to-end suites all run in CI.
- `cairn doctor` and `cairn status` report capture health, spool depth, the
  oldest undelivered entry, and a closed, ordered vocabulary of reasons delivery
  is blocked.

## Supported platforms

| Platform | Status |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple silicon, `aarch64-apple-darwin`) | Supported |
| macOS (Intel, `x86_64-apple-darwin`) | Supported |
| Linux (`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`) | Supported |
| Linux (`aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`) | Supported |
| Windows (`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) | Supported |

The integration suites run on all three operating systems in CI.

## Upgrading from alpha.5

`cairn update` fetches and replaces both binaries for you. It does not restart
the daemon — it prints the two commands below, and you run them:

```bash
cairn daemon stop && cairn daemon start
```

Your local state is kept. The local store gains migrations, applied on first
start, and existing integrations are adopted rather than replaced.

**If you run your own server, upgrade the server first.** The server's schema
advances with this release, and an older server cannot serve a newer client's
requests. The server applies its migrations on start.

```bash
docker compose pull && docker compose up -d
```

**Autonomous capture is on after the upgrade.** Cairn will begin recording the
work your connected agents do and consolidating it into durable knowledge. If
you want to see what it holds before trusting it:

```bash
cairn status
cairn doctor
```

Nothing is sent anywhere you have not linked. With no server configured, capture
and consolidation stay entirely local.

## Compatibility

- **Server and client versions must match across this boundary.** A client on
  alpha.6 talking to a server on alpha.5 will be refused rather than silently
  degraded. Upgrade the server first.
- Knowledge written by alpha.5 remains readable. Records created before this
  release carry no autonomous provenance, which is correct — nothing observed
  them being created.
- Cairn is pre-1.0. Storage schemas and the wire protocol may still change
  without a deprecation period.

## Install

Download the archive for your platform, verify it, and put the binaries on your
PATH. `cairn` and `cairnd` must live in the same directory — `cairn` starts the
daemon itself.

macOS and Linux:

```bash
VERSION=0.1.0-alpha.6
TARGET=aarch64-apple-darwin   # or x86_64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu

curl -fsSLO https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/releases/download/v${VERSION}/cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}.tar.gz
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/releases/download/v${VERSION}/SHA256SUMS
sha256sum --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS

tar -xzf cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}.tar.gz
sudo install -m 0755 cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}/cairn cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}/cairnd /usr/local/bin/
```

Windows, in PowerShell — the archive is a `.zip`:

```powershell
$VERSION = "0.1.0-alpha.6"
$TARGET = "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"

Invoke-WebRequest "https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/releases/download/v$VERSION/cairn-v$VERSION-$TARGET.zip" -OutFile cairn.zip
Invoke-WebRequest "https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/releases/download/v$VERSION/SHA256SUMS" -OutFile SHA256SUMS

Expand-Archive cairn.zip -DestinationPath .
mkdir "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Cairn" -Force
Copy-Item "cairn-v$VERSION-$TARGET\cairn.exe","cairn-v$VERSION-$TARGET\cairnd.exe" "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Cairn"
setx PATH "$env:PATH;$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Cairn"
```

Open a new terminal so the PATH change takes effect. Then, inside a Git
repository, on any platform:

```bash
cairn init
cairn agents
cairn connect claude-code   # or codex, or opencode
```

## Container images

Only the server-side components ship as images. The local agent is native by
design.

```
ghcr.io/vellixia/cairn-server:0.1.0-alpha.6
ghcr.io/vellixia/cairn-web:0.1.0-alpha.6
```

Both are also published under an immutable `sha-<short-sha>` tag and built for
`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. There is deliberately no `latest` tag for a
pre-release. An example stack is in
[`deploy/docker-compose.yml`](https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/blob/main/deploy/docker-compose.yml).

## Verifying what you downloaded

- `SHA256SUMS` covers every archive, `.tar.gz` and `.zip` alike.
- `SBOM.spdx.json` describes the release contents.
- Archives and images carry GitHub build provenance attestations:

```bash
gh attestation verify cairn-v0.1.0-alpha.6-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip --repo Vellixia/Cairn
```

## Known limitations

- **Alpha.** Expect defects. Do not depend on this for anything you cannot
  afford to lose.
- **Accuracy of autonomous records is reviewed, not asserted.** Cairn's own tests
  prove that records exist, that their provenance resolves to the session's own
  accepted events, and that no ungrounded word from a prompt reaches a durable
  record. Whether a claim is *right* is judged by an independent reviewer, and
  this release does not claim otherwise.
- **OpenCode produces structural knowledge only.** It has no stable, documented
  completion boundary for settled assistant messages, so Cairn declines to read
  semantic signals from it rather than guess. Capture and consolidation work; a
  decision you state in OpenCode is not recorded as one.
- **OpenCode cannot reach `automatic` continuity.** It publishes no
  post-compaction session open. `agent_initiated` is the truthful answer, and a
  deterministic mechanism is tracked in
  [#49](https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/issues/49).
- **Topic keys do not converge across agents.** Value keys do. Two agents
  recording the same fact tend to agree on the value and disagree on the
  namespace, which costs deduplication rather than correctness.
- **Consolidation runs on the server.** With no server linked, capture and local
  knowledge work, and durable consolidated knowledge does not accumulate.
